verdicts.title: Counting Algebraic Curves with Tropical Geometry
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Tropical geometry is a piecewise linear "shadow" of algebraic geometry. It allows for the computation of several cohomological invariants of an algebraic variety. In particular, its application to enumerative algebraic geometry led to significant progress.

There is no mention of circuits, complexity, or rank in the computational sense relevant to the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Note on $p$-adic Local Functional Equation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Given primes $\ell\ne p$, we record here a $p$-adic valued Fourier theory on a local field over $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$, which is developed under the perspective of group schemes. As an application, by substituting rigid analysis for complex analysis, it leads naturally to the $p$-adic local functional equation at $\ell$, which strongly resembles the complex one in Tate's thesis.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses $p$-adic valued Fourier theory on local fields and a $p$-adic local functional equation, which relates to harmonic analysis and number theory, but does not mention tropical geometry, Boolean functions, AC0 circuits, or circuit complexity. The concepts are mathematically related at a high level (e.g., $p$-adic numbers) but the specific claim about minimal rank of tropicalized Boolean functions and AC0 parity circuit size is not addressed or implied.
